name: Ranipuram Hills
tagline: Shola forests, rolling grasslands and short treks — best in the dry season
summary: Ranipuram is Kasaragod’s cool hill station (≈750 m) of shola forests, meadows and short trekking trails. Dry-season treks from November improve views and wildlife visibility.
description: Ranipuram Hills (formerly Madathumala) is a compact Western-Ghats hill station in Panathady, Vellarikundu taluk, Kasaragod. The area combines evergreen shola patches, monsoon forests and open grassland meadows and is managed as an ecotourism/forest area.

It matters because Ranipuram is the highest point in Kasaragod and a biodiversity hotspot — an ecological corridor that links Kerala forests to the Talacauvery/Coorg highlands of Karnataka. The hills hold rare shola vegetation, rich birdlife and a range of mammals.

Visitors get a short, scenic trek (round trip about 5 km) that moves from closed-canopy forest into vast shola grasslands and panoramic viewpoints. The site is compact and walker-friendly: expect cool air, mist early and late, and good sightings of birds and mammals when the weather is drier.
highlights: Distinct shola forests and lemongrass-dominated meadows
Short 2.5 km one-way trek (≈5 km round trip) with multiple viewpoints
High bird diversity — hornbills, paradise flycatcher and grassland species
Part of the Panathady reserve that merges with Talacauvery/Coorg forests
Good chance of wildlife sightings (elephants, sambar, Malabar giant squirrel)

sections.heading: Background
body: Ranipuram sits on the Western Ghats close to the Kerala–Karnataka border; base elevation is commonly cited at about 750 m with the summit higher (peak reported around 1,048 m). The place was historically known as Madathumala and is now a small ecotourism hill station administered in partnership with the forest department and local tourism bodies.
Ecologically it contains rare shola pockets among grasslands and monsoon forest; researchers working at Ranipuram have recorded new insect/faunal records, underlining the area’s conservation value.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Trek the official trail from the forest check post (trail ~2.5 km one way). The walk begins under a dense canopy and opens into sweeping shola grasslands and viewpoints that look toward the Coorg–Talacauvery ranges.

Birdwatching is a major draw (great hornbill, Malabar grey hornbill, paradise flycatcher among others) and the grassland/forest matrix is good for mammal sightings — elephants, sambar, gaurs, jungle cat and Malabar giant squirrel have been reported. Short jeep rides from Panathady and simple cottages/eco-stays in the area support overnight visits.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best season is the drier, cool months (local sources list October–March as favourable). From November onward the weather typically dries after the monsoon and visibility and wildlife activity for daytime treks usually improve — still expect morning mist and variable conditions.

Nearest railhead is Kanhangad (about 43–49 km depending on route); Mangalore International Airport is the closest major airport (~113 km by road). The trek begins near the Panathady forest check post (about 9 km from Panathady town). Entry, fees and daily timings are managed by forest/park authorities — confirm latest opening hours and entry rules before you go.

latest.text: Parappa (Panathady area) government page updated (Oct 31, 2026) reiterates Ranipuram’s importance, gives trekking details (total ≈5 km) and lists best visiting season as October–March.

Onmanorama published a detailed trek guide (Oct 24, 2026) noting the trail round trip ≈5 km, published entry fees (₹60 adult, ₹25 child) and that the hill is open 08:00–17:30 while trail entry closes at 15:00; visitors must return by 17:30.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November–March (cooler, drier period — clearer views and better daytime wildlife visibility)
visitorInfo.howToReach: Drive or take bus to Panathady (from Kanhangad about 43–49 km), then continue 9 km to the Forest check post; nearest railway station Kanhangad, nearest major airport Mangalore (≈113 km). Confirm local bus/jeep timings at Kanhangad/Panathady before travel.
etiquette: Start early and finish well before the trail closing time; confirm current trail hours and entry fees with forest/DTPC sources.
Wear good-grip trekking shoes, carry water and basic first aid; trails get slippery in rain and leeches are common during/soon after monsoon.
Keep to the designated trail — straying can get you lost and disturbs wildlife; do not feed animals or dispose plastic in the forest.
Mobile signal can be unreliable; tell someone your plan and carry a power bank and a printed map or local directions.
